elements.quote: Knowledge on the sequelae of Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) remains limited due to the relatively recent onset of this pathology.
elements.reason: States the current state of knowledge as limited, but does not explicitly describe important uncertainties beyond that limitation.

elements.quote: To determine the prevalence of respiratory symptoms in survivors of hospital admission after COVID-19 infection.
elements.reason: Clearly explains the need for conducting the review by stating the purpose to determine prevalence of relevant symptoms.

No evidence is provided that discusses the existence of similar systematic reviews or explains the need for the current review in relation to prior work (including updates/replications with citations).
This review concerns prevalence of symptoms (not an intervention effect), so a proposed mechanism of action for an intervention is not applicable.
The criterion applies to complex interventions/delivery contexts; the provided evidence describes a prevalence/literature synthesis rather than a complex intervention with components and outcomes.
The retrieved evidence does not provide an explicit statement of the review’s objective(s) or question(s) (e.g., no stated objective/question in an abstract/introduction).

elements.quote: We conducted a systematic review of the literature using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) (25). The review was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO) (CRD42020215533)
elements.reason: The provided evidence does not indicate that this is a review of intervention effects, so the requirement to state planned intervention comparisons using PICO is not applicable based on the retrieved material.

elements.quote: The inclusion criteria for the systematic review were a) randomised controlled trials (RCT) and observational studies (retrospective, prospective, crosssectional, longitudinal, case-control and cohort), b) whose objective was to determine the prevalence of respiratory symptoms in patients presenting with COVID-19, c) laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 infection by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) or polymerase chain reaction dual fluorescence (PCR), d) hospitalised adult patients ( \u0015 18 years), e) follow-up from 30 days after Covid-19 infection, f) follow-up from 21 days after hospital discharge.
elements.reason: The review specifies multiple study characteristics for eligibility (eligible study designs, lab-confirmed COVID-19, hospitalised adults, and follow-up timing). However, it does not clearly specify all relevant “question-framework” components in the form PRISMA expects (e.g., full participant/outcome framework details), so coverage is incomplete.
No evidence was retrieved specifying eligibility criteria for report characteristics such as dissemination year, language, or publication/report status.

elements.quote: 17 articles were excluded due to wrong outcome ( n ¼ 6), wrong population ( n ¼ 5), wrong study design ( n ¼ 4), duplicate data ( n ¼ 1) and for being preprint ( n ¼ 1).
elements.reason: Although exclusions include “wrong outcome,” the evidence does not distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured versus exclusion because outcome results were not reported.
No evidence was retrieved describing the groups used in each synthesis and how those groups are linked to the review objectives/comparisons.

elements.quote: No other restrictions in eligibility criteria were applied.
elements.reason: The evidence indicates there were no additional eligibility restrictions beyond those listed, but it does not provide rationales for any notable restrictions on study eligibility.

elements.quote: The search covered the period from December 2019 to October 22, 2020.
elements.reason: A date for the end of the database search period (October 22, 2020) is reported.
